title: Multilang SDK streaming & retry scenario compiler for deterministic contract fixtures
creator: Maya R. Chen
description: Goal: produce a portable 'scenario compiler' that ingests live SDK traces from Python, TypeScript, and Go SDKs (streaming + retry events) and outputs deterministic VCR-style fixtures and contract assertions against the Redwood API. The compiler should: 1) canonicalize language-specific streaming frames into a platform-neutral event model (message-chunk, token-delta, metadata, retry-marker, error-signal), 2) support deterministic replays that simulate partial responses, connection drops, and retry backoffs, 3) generate compact fixtures with optional token-level diffs for eval suites, and 4) emit contract test artifacts (expected HTTP/HTTP2 exchange, header assertions, response schema checks). Why: current SDK replay tooling is fragmented by language and does not capture subtle streaming/retry interleavings that cause production regressions (e.g., partial chunk reorder when backpressure + retry happens). This ticket scopes the compiler core, fixtures format, and a first-pass conversion of existing Python/TS recorded traces into deterministic fixtures for CI contract tests.
acceptance_criteria: 1) Compiler accepts raw traces from Python/TS/Go SDKs and produces a canonical .scenario fixture that replays deterministically under the mockserver harness. 2) Replays support injection of: connection drop, 5xx, and simulated latency; SDK retry policies exercise expected retry count and backoff. 3) CI job runs the generated fixtures against the Redwood staging API and produces pass/fail contract assertions. 4) Documentation + example conversion for one Python and one TypeScript streaming trace. 5) Size of canonicalized fixtures limited to <5x raw trace size by default with optional full-token mode.
notes: Initial spike showed canonical model works when we normalize: (seq_id, event_type, payload, is_terminal, provenance_sdk, checkpoint_id). We experimented with two serialization formats: newline-delimited JSON events (human readable, larger) and a compressed binary protobuf (compact, harder to inspect). Decided to default to NDJSON for ease of debugging and tooling, with an optional --compress flag to emit gzipped protobuf for CI storage. Token-level diffs are expensive; we'll gate full-token fixtures behind a project label 'eval' and default to message-chunk diffs for regular contract tests.
comments: 2026-02-16 - Maya: Kickoff meeting with SDK leads (Priya, Tomas) to collect trace schemas from Python/TS/Go. Action: provide 3 representative streaming traces per SDK by 2026-02-20.

2026-02-20 - Tomas N.: Uploaded TS/Browser trace set and noted that the browser SDK coalesces chunks differently than node. Logged an item to normalize 'chunk_boundary' vs 'byte_length' in canonicalizer.

2026-02-23 - Design review: agreed on NDJSON canonical events + optional gzip; Daniel to prototype compiler CLI (go binary) that reads raw trace dir and emits .scenario fixtures. Decision: include 'sdk_version' and 'tokenizer_name' metadata on fixtures.

2026-02-28 - Daniel K.: Prototype v0 converts 7 traces (3 py, 3 ts, 1 go) and generates fixtures. Found flaky replay behavior caused by missing 'retry_marker' when SDK retried without closing stream. Added support for explicit 'retry_marker' events and checkpoint_id mapping in replay engine.

2026-03-02 - Review feedback from QA (Anika): replays must preserve wire-level headers (x-request-id, authorization redaction rules). Added header-redaction step in compiler with allowlist for test-only headers.

2026-03-04 - PR 348 submitted. Tests: local mockserver runs 12 generated fixtures; 2 failed due to tokenization mismatch between library tokenizers. Plan: add tokenizer mapping table and a 'normalize_tokens' pass before emitting token diffs.

2026-03-05 - Action items: (1) Daniel to add tokenizer mapping and update README; (2) Maya to add CI job in sdk-test-harness to run newly generated fixtures nightly against staging; (3) PM to notify integrators for canary run the week of 2026-03-15.
Future follow-ups: instrument fixture generation to include optional per-chunk latency histogram for better replay fidelity; consider integrating with e2e infra for dedicated capacity smoke tests.
qa_plan: 1) Unit tests for canonicalizer with edge-case traces (empty-chunk, multi-retry). 2) Integration: run fixtures in mockserver harness (docker) and assert SDK behavior matches recorded outcome. 3) Contract: generated assertions run against staging Redwood API; failures triaged and traced back to fixture normalization. 4) Include cross-lang smoke tests: Python/TS/Go clients replay the same .scenario and must observe consistent terminal state.
risks_and_mitigations: Risk: tokenization differences across SDKs can make exact token-level fixtures brittle. Mitigation: default to message-chunk diffs and add tokenizer-normalization; surface token-diff only for eval-labeled fixtures. Risk: large fixtures bloat CI. Mitigation: gzip option and fixture retention policy plus selective sampling for nightly runs.
next_steps: 1) Merge PR 348 after addressing tokenizer mapping comment. 2) Add nightly CI job and run the sample fixtures to collect flaky rates. 3) Convert an additional 50 historical traces from production staging for broader coverage. 4) Draft short RFC for fixture format and lifecycle policy.
